proposed_features.description: The primary coloration of the plumage, which is the most obvious visual difference between the groups, separating the brownish birds from the black ones.
The geometry of the bill, distinguishing the short, conical bills of the smaller birds from the long, heavy, and often hooked bills of the larger corvids.
The shape of the tail feathers when closed, which varies from a rounded or square end to a distinct wedge shape.
The apparent size of the bird relative to its perch or environment, separating the small passerines from the large corvids.
The length of the legs relative to the body, which is noticeably longer in the larger corvids compared to the smaller birds.
The profile of the head, distinguishing the rounded, small heads of the smaller birds from the larger, more angular heads of the corvids.
The visual texture of the feathers, ranging from smooth and sleek to shaggy or fluffy, particularly around the neck and chest.
The color of the iris, which is dark in the smaller birds and often lighter (yellow or white) in the larger corvids.
The color of the bill, which is dark in most birds but can be pale or yellowish in some individuals.
The length of the wings relative to the tail, which is longer in the larger corvids and shorter in the smaller birds.
The overall body shape, distinguishing the compact, rounded bodies of the smaller birds from the elongated, robust bodies of the corvids.
The length of the neck, which is short in the smaller birds and longer in the larger corvids.
